title: Tenant-sliced rollforward & live-patch plan for sticky canary regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers reported silent quality degradation during a staged model rollout in hosted and dedicated environments. Root cause analysis shows a combination of: a subtle tokenization mapping change in the new model variant, inconsistent KV cache reconciliation across routing slices, and an edge case in the live-traffic router that misrouted ~0.4% of requests to the new variant outside the canary slice. Several customers opened escalations; one enterprise tenant saw amplified hallucination rates triggering an on-call incident. This ticket defines a tenant-sliced rollforward (live-patch) strategy that avoids full rollback, minimizes blast radius, and gives a predictable communication and remediation path for Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.
steps: 1) Rapid containment: immediately quarantine affected model variant from cross-tenant routing and pin all high-risk tenants to previous stable model (actioned by traffic-control team).
2) Snapshot state: capture KV cache snapshots and routing metadata for affected nodes before any stateful changes (SRE leads: Marco Silva).
3) Patch path: prepare a live patch that rewrites tokenization compatibility shim in serving runtime; deploy to a single tenant-slice for verification.
4) Rollforward strategy: staged expansion of the patch using tenant-slicing with traffic proportions (1%, 10%, 50%) and gating on quality metrics.
5) KV cache reconciliation: invalidate per-tenant prefix caches and execute controlled warmup procedure to avoid cold-start artefacts.
6) Fallback mechanism: automated immediate pin-to-stable for any tenant crossing degradation thresholds; alert on misroute counts > 0.1% for more than 5 minutes.
7) Customer communications: coordinate CS/SE to send templated messages and provide drift diagnostics for impacted tenants.
8) Post-release validation: run replayed production traces through patched variant in isolated environment before mass expansion.
9) Metrics & dashboards: add short-lived dashboards to monitor BLEU/ROUGE-like quality proxies, hallucination-rate proxy, latency P99, and misroute rate at tenant granularity.
10) Postmortem and automation: extract a checklist for future rollouts and implement a preflight gating rule in the orchestration controller.

rollback_criteria: If hallucination proxy increases by >30% relative to baseline for any tenant after expansion for 15 consecutive minutes.
If misroute rate exceeds 0.2% sustained for more than 10 minutes during any expansion step.
If latency P99 increases >40% for tenant slice post-patch and does not recover within 10 minutes.
Explicit customer request to revert (treated as P0).
success_criteria: Stable or improved hallucination proxy for all expanded tenant slices for 72 hours.
Misroute rate <= 0.05% across all production clusters for 7 days.
No high-severity customer escalations linked to the variant for 14 days.
Automated preflight check (router hash parity + tokenization compatibility test) added to CI for future rollouts.
postmortem_actions: 1) Submit automation ticket to add router-hash parity check into rollout orchestration (ENG-117254 planned).
2) Add a KV-cache reconciliation utility to orchestration controller to run as part of model swap.
3) Update runbook with tenant-slice expansion percentages and explicit gating thresholds.
4) Schedule customer-facing follow-up session with AcmeFin to review findings and remediation.
5) Add compile-time check in tokenizer library to prevent incompatible tokenization bundles from entering model catalog.
communication_templates: Initial inbound: 'We are investigating a quality regression observed after a recent model rollout. We've isolated traffic and are applying a targeted fix. We'll share updates every 8 hours and provide per-tenant diagnostics.'

Post-containment: 'Containment complete: affected model quarantined and your tenant has been pinned to the previous stable variant. We are running a staged repair and will update you when we expand the validated patch.'

Post-resolution: 'We believe the issue is resolved. Attached is a short report with root cause analysis, mitigations performed, and actions taken to prevent recurrence. Please schedule a review with our SRE/SE team if you'd like deeper instrumentation.'
